recorded: Every case passed against both originals: the JavaScript versions with Node.js 26.12.1, run as node {program}.js, and the Python versions with Python 3.15.2, run as python3 with the program's hyphens turned into underscores, as in python3 $(echo {program}.py | tr - _). Every program uses only the standard library and takes no arguments. The relevance, cleaning, and PII tools are deterministic, so their demos are compared exactly, with the PII gate's prose with or without accents, since the Python version writes it without them, and O(n²) or O(n^2) in the cleaning note, while their self-check reports must end with the same totals and the titles of the checks are free. The extraction tool runs the tesseract CLI, which the recording machine lacked, so its first case ran in a Debian trixie container with tesseract 5.5.0, tesseract-ocr-por 4.1.0 (the fast model), Node.js 20.19.2, and Python 3.13.5. That container read the same text as the dataset-amplitude-seguros.jsonl the lesson ships, which Homebrew's tesseract wrote, the first plate as QJk-4F82 included, with confidences up to 0.6 points apart, so each confidence is compared within 1.5 points and the plate's k in either case. Its second case puts a stand-in tesseract on PATH that fails as tesseract does without the Portuguese model, with the message that container printed, and ran on the host. The multimodal tool calls Gemini on Vertex AI at a hardcoded regional address, so the copy that produced these cases reads GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL instead, a one-line change in each version, and the cases set GCP_PROJECT_ID to a placeholder project and answer gcloud auth print-access-token with a stand-in that prints a placeholder token, which the replay requires as the bearer token. No Google Cloud project was available, and Ollama does not serve Vertex AI's format, so every answer is synthesized from Vertex AI's documented generateContent format: the first case carries the twelve correct fields and the token usage that the lesson's ocr-vs-llm-extracao-comparativo.md reports for gemini-2.5-flash (2,384 input and about 40 output tokens per document), the second a misread plate, a wrong amount, and fields that differ from the key only in accents and case, and the third Vertex AI's documented 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for the last document, while the failing gcloud prints what gcloud prints without an active account. Requests are compared by the prompt, the image's length and last bytes, the mime type, temperature 0, and responseMimeType, with inline_data or inlineData, and latencies are free. The Python version prints its extracted JSON with spaces, writes whole amounts as 7940.0, quotes a failed field's values with Python's repr, names its own OCR counterpart in the closing line, and prints its final error to standard output where JavaScript uses standard error, so the patterns accept either and that error line is not compared.
